body: The part of tokenized equities I track is the plumbing. Ondo opened an in-kind route this week: approved institutions can convert shares they already hold into its tokenized stocks via Alpaca's network, not cash first. Less financing friction, and a cheaper second input into primary minting. Caveats: Ethereum and BNB Chain only, case by case, no fee schedule or minimum size published. Ask who can use a new rail, what it costs, how you exit. Views are personal.

Eligible xStocks holders can now sign in to Broadridge's ProxyVote.com with Web3 credentials, review proxy materials and submit vote preferences. ① Governance is routed through existing proxy infrastructure, not voted natively on-chain, where a vote's legal effect is unsettled in most jurisdictions. ② The bridge is partial: no word on what share of holders is in scope, and the product is not sold to US or UK persons. Test: who may vote, what it attaches to, whether it binds. Not advice.
